transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just... I can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I’ll start talking to someone about an overnight shift at work, and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, or... paint colors, or patient charts. I can just see everyone getting completely lost when I try to talk to them.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually high, energetic, or irritable compared to your normal self?

No, I haven't felt like that. I mean, I definitely don't have any extra energy, and I haven't felt high or anything. I don't think I've been unusually irritable, either. I just haven't noticed feeling that way at all.
About how long have you been having this trouble keeping your thoughts and words in order?

I think it's been... about a year and a month now. That's when the trouble with my thoughts really started happening. And honestly, it's the same amount of time I've been dealing with this... this feeling that I'm being watched. So yeah, both of those things have been going on for about a year and one month.
During this past year, have you had periods where you felt consistently down, depressed, or unable to enjoy things?

Yeah, I have. Honestly, most days I just feel... heavy and empty right from the time I wake up. And it doesn't really lift. A lot of times, after my shifts are over, I'll just sit in my car crying for a while before I can even bring myself to drive home.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty, and depressed mood?
It's been about a year and two months. Yeah, the depression and just... not having any interest in things, it's been with me for about a year and two months now.

During this past year, was there ever a period of at least two weeks where your depression lifted and you felt your normal mood, but you still felt watched or had trouble keeping your thoughts straight?

Yeah, there was a time like that. Um... it was a stretch of a few weeks where I actually wasn't in that deep, depressed place. I felt a bit more normal, mood-wise. But even then, I still believed the cameras and supervisors were monitoring me. I couldn't shake that feeling, and I kept acting really guarded at work because of it. So the depression lifted for a bit, but the other stuff didn't.
